title: Principal and inferior officers
summary: Inferior officers hold positions whose responsibilities and relationship to superior officials permit the alternative appointment methods authorized by Article II.
notes:
Morrison considers removal by a higher official, limited duties, limited jurisdiction, and temporary tenure. Edmond centers on direction and supervision by Senate-confirmed officers, including administrative control and executive appellate review. Arthrex holds that final patent adjudications insulated from principal-officer review were incompatible with the appointment method used for the administrative patent judges.

These decisions should be compared on their actual institutional arrangements. Neither Edmond nor Arthrex announces an exclusive criterion covering every office, and Arthrex expressly limits its supervision discussion to the adjudicative context presented. Being lower on an organizational chart is relevant but does not alone establish that constitutionally sufficient supervision exists.
